subject: Recap & intake: SparkBridge trial — prompt/log harvest, acceptance criteria, next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@sparkbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:10:00Z
Subject: Recap & intake: SparkBridge trial — prompt/log harvest, acceptance criteria, next steps

Hi Asha / Devon — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed intake plan so we have a shared checklist for the trial kickoff. We captured the goals and risks from the discussion; please flag anything I missed.

Goals (agreed):
- Validate LLM-assisted triage for support tickets (precision on intent classification >= 88% for top-1).
- Ensure latency target: 95th percentile < 350ms for single-turn generation at median ticket length.
- Confirm data controls: customer-owned S3, no retention beyond trial window unless agreed.

Minimum success criteria (POC acceptance):
1) Accuracy: labeled eval set yields >= 88% top-1 intent accuracy and <= 8% critical-mislabel rate.
2) Latency: 95p < 350ms in Redwood Dedicated config (as measured by Redwood Console).
3) Integration: ability to pull prompt/log bundles from your S3 bucket and produce a reproducible eval report.

What we need from SparkBridge (deliverables):
- Prompt/log bundle (CSV preferred) with columns: request_id, user_text, context, expected_label, severity_flag. Example attached as sparkbridge_prompt_samples.csv.
- PII mapping spreadsheet showing which fields contain PII and intended redaction/anonymization approach (sparkbridge_pii_mapping.xlsx).
- Any short prompt templates you want tested (few-shot examples).

Intake options (pick one):
A) Upload to s3://sparkbridge-uploads/poc/prompts/ (we can provide presigned URLs)
B) Share a Google Drive folder with the files
C) For small sets, email CSV directly (only for <500 rows)

Proposed timeline:
- Aug 8: Customer uploads prompt/log bundle (target)
- Aug 9–12: Redwood triage + pre-processing; quick sync if questions
- Aug 13–20: Run evaluation harness, baseline metrics, and two model variants
- Aug 22: Delivery of POC report + recommended next steps

Owners / next steps:
- SparkBridge: Asha (content + upload), Devon (security point-of-contact)
- Redwood: Ben (sales/POC lead), Marissa (CS owner), Karthik (evaluation & model config)

Attachments: trial-eval-checklist.pdf (intake checklist), sparkbridge_prompt_samples.csv (sample schema)

If this looks good I will: 1) create the HubSpot engagement, 2) provision a presigned S3 prefix for you, and 3) loop in Marissa/Karthik to schedule the technical kickoff.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Cc: Devon King <devon.king@sparkbridge.ai>
Date: 2027-08-02T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap & intake: SparkBridge trial — prompt/log harvest, acceptance criteria, next steps

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with our expectations. A few clarifying items before we upload: 

1) PII / redaction: we have email, user_id (hashed), and free-text descriptions. We can anonymize emails and keep user_id hashed. Do you need a sample mapping template? (I attached a small CSV of 150 rows we can use as a test).
2) Tokenization / max length: our average ticket length is ~180 tokens, 95p at 400 tokens. Will Redwood truncate or do progressive chunking?
3) Model variants: can you run both a smaller 8B quantized variant and a 70B float baseline? We want cost/latency vs quality comparison.

We prefer option A (S3 upload). Please send presigned upload links and an S3 prefix. We'll aim to upload by EOD Aug 8.

Attaching: sparkbridge_prompt_samples.csv (sample 150 rows).

Thanks,
Asha Patel
Head of Product, SparkBridge
asha.patel@sparkbridge.ai

Subject: Re: Recap & intake: SparkBridge trial — prompt/log harvest, acceptance criteria, next steps

Hi Asha — great, thanks for the sample. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) PII / redaction: we have email, user_id (hashed), and free-text descriptions.
We recommend you replace email addresses with a token (e.g., <EMAIL>) and keep hashed user_id. The attached sparkbridge_pii_mapping.xlsx is a short template — fill the column "pii_type" and "recommended_action". We will not persist raw fields beyond the trial evaluation unless you explicitly request retention.

> 2) Tokenization / max length: our runtime supports adaptive chunking for long contexts but for single-turn evals we will pass up to 1024 tokens to the model by default. If you'd like progressive chunking for very long threads we can enable that in the evaluation config (flag: progressive_chunking=true).

> 3) Model variants: yes — we will run the 8B quantized variant (cost-optimized) and the 70B float baseline. We will report latency and quality side-by-side in the POC report.

S3 upload: I created a temporary prefix and will send presigned PUT links via a secure email with instructions in the next message. Prefix: s3://redwood-uploads/sparkbridge-poc-202708/ (we will isolate and expire access after Aug 31).

Next internal steps on our side: Marissa will schedule the technical kickoff (once you confirm upload), and Karthik will prepare the eval harness (classification schema + metrics).

I'll follow up with the presigned links in a separate email.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
